thread:
Priya (support): FYI customer acme-prod reporting lots of 401s + high p95 (300-800ms) since ~08:10 UTC. They say EU traffic is landing in us-west. Ticket CS-4829. logs: https://redwood.inc/err/CS-4829 :eyes:
Mike (eng): Can you paste a sample request_id + a minimal curl so we can trace?
Priya (support): sample req id `req_0x9a12f3`

Headers snippet:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx
Host: api.redwood.com
User-Agent: acme-client/1.2.0
X-Forwarded-For: 93.184.216.34
```
Response: `401 {"error":"invalid_token"}` but only when coming from customer EU office.
Jake (sre): did a quick dig/traceroute from my laptop -> dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com => 3.4.5.6 (us-west edge). traceroute to 3.4.5.6 shows hops into us-west cloud. Looks like resolver returns a US anycast answer for that EU resolver. Likely ISP caching / missing EDNS. TTL on DNS is 300 but some resolvers sticky beyond TTL.
Anita (infra): we had a geodb push yesterday 02:12 UTC; one FRA rack failed to index due to transient S3 permission errors, fixed 03:05 UTC. That could cause stale fallback mappings on some edge clusters if they read an older geo DB. I'm pulling sync logs now.
Priya (support): customer needs workaround ASAP, they're getting retry storms and billing noise. What's the customer-safe mitigation?
Mike (eng): short-term: ask customer to use regional endpoint `eu.api.redwood.com` (no anycast) or include `X-Region: eu` header to bias routing. We'll also add a temporary routing override for prefixes that we see from that ISP. Creating runbook entry now.
Lydia (billing): opened billing case BILL-789 for ACME to review retry charges and issued provisional credit. Keep me posted if they continue to get charged.
Jake (sre): repro steps I used to confirm -> run these from an EU residential ISP to reproduce:
```
# DNS check
dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com +short
# EDNS detail
dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com +nocomments +noquestion +noanswer +ttlid +edns
# traceroute
traceroute -n $(dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com)
```
Check if the resolver strips ECS or if NAT causes wrong client subnet. If you see a US IP, file resolver probe with the ISP and ask them to clear cache.
Anita (infra): I'm pushing a retry of the geodb sync for the FRA rack and reindexing routing table; if successful we'll invalidate route caches and bump the CDN mapping TTL to 60s for an hour to force refresh.
ops-bot: route-change RC-1023 created by Mike (canary to eu edges, scope: affected prefixes). Status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Priya (support): thanks all — I'll send the eu.endpoint workaround and the repro steps to the customer, share BILL-789 number. tagging @Lydia for follow-up.
Mike (eng): long-term we should add a customer-visible region header in the API docs and a hint for resolvers without ECS. Also log resolver IP and EDNS info in request metadata (PII-safe) so support can triage faster.
Jake (sre): adding note to incident: likely cause = ISP resolver cache + transient geodb sync glitch -> cross-region routing -> auth failures because token realm mapping/edge config differs. Mitigation = regional endpoint + route override + geodb reindex.
Priya (support): closing loop — customer accepted eu.api.redwood.com workaround, watching for regressions. Will report back after RC-1023 completes. :white_check_mark:
